name: When is a low threshold shower the best choice for accessibility?

mainEntity.name: When is a low threshold shower the best choice for accessibility?

acceptedAnswer.text: Low threshold showers are ideal for aging-in-place homeowners, individuals with temporary injuries, or anyone wanting easier daily bathroom access without a massive remodel. If a family member struggles to lift their legs over a 14-to-18-inch bathtub edge, swapping to a low curb removes a primary fall risk. It is also an excellent choice for smaller bathrooms where a complete zero-clearance, curbless shower is structurally impractical due to joist depth or plumbing constraints.
acceptedAnswer.description: It is best when stepping over high tub walls becomes difficult or hazardous, especially in bathrooms where structural limits prevent curbless designs.
